projects.name: Quantum Aggregate Signature for VANET
projects.description: Independent reproduction of a 2025 research paper on quantum aggregate signatures for vehicular networks. Built a quantum simulator in Python/NumPy (BB84 QKD, entanglement-based signatures, aggregation, teleportation), formally verified the protocol with Scyther — 17/17 secrecy and agreement claims, finding and repairing an attack in the authors' own model — and reproduced the performance evaluation in OMNeT++ with 46 vehicles and zero message loss. Also uncovered a public-forgery weakness in the published scheme and proposed a hardened variant.
projects.details:
An independent reproduction of a 2025 research paper proposing quantum aggregate signatures for Vehicular Ad-hoc Networks (VANETs) — where cars must authenticate each other at highway speed, with classical cryptography struggling under the overhead.

I rebuilt the entire scheme from scratch: a Python/NumPy quantum simulator implementing BB84 Quantum Key Distribution, entanglement-based aggregate signatures, the aggregation step itself, and quantum teleportation — all covered by a pytest suite.

The protocol was formally verified with Scyther: all 17 secrecy and agreement claims passed, and along the way I found and repaired an actual attack in the authors' own model. I then reproduced the performance evaluation in OMNeT++ with 46 vehicles and zero message loss.

The highlight: I uncovered a public-forgery weakness in the published scheme and proposed a hardened variant — turning a reproduction project into original cryptanalysis.

projects.name: Smart Campus Lost & Found Portal
projects.description: Full-stack portal that automatically matches lost and found reports across a 5,000+ student campus. JWT authentication, Cloudinary photo uploads, a cosine-similarity matching engine with an 80%+ match rate, real-time Socket.IO chat to arrange handovers and a Recharts analytics dashboard. Deployed on Vercel/Render with sub-2s page loads.
projects.details:
Losing things on a 5,000+ student campus is inevitable — but the notice boards weren't cutting it. This portal automates the match between "I lost X" and "I found X" reports.

At its core is a cosine-similarity matching engine that compares lost and found reports (title, description, category, location) and automatically surfaces likely matches the moment a new report is posted — achieving an 80%+ match rate in testing.

The stack: JWT authentication for secure accounts, Cloudinary for photo uploads, Socket.IO for real-time chat so finders and losers can arrange handovers instantly, and a Recharts analytics dashboard showing lost/found trends across the campus.

It's fully deployed — frontend on Vercel, backend on Render — with sub-2-second page loads, and was built as a real utility students could actually use.

projects.name: AI Code Reviewer
projects.description: AI-powered code review platform — paste code and get instant feedback. Monaco Editor (the editor behind VS Code) in the browser, Groq's LLaMA 3.3 70B for fast reviews, Piston API for sandboxed multi-language execution and Socket.IO for real-time updates. Frontend on Vercel, backend on Render.
projects.details:
An AI pair reviewer that lives in your browser: paste code, get instant, structured feedback on correctness, style and potential bugs.

The editor is Monaco — the same component that powers VS Code — so the coding experience feels native, with syntax highlighting and language support out of the box. Reviews are generated by Groq's LLaMA 3.3 70B, whose API returns responses fast enough to feel like a live conversation about your code.

Code can also be executed safely through the Piston API in a sandboxed multi-language runtime, so you can verify a fix without leaving the platform. Socket.IO streams both reviews and execution results in real time.

Built on the MERN stack, deployed frontend-on-Vercel / backend-on-Render — a tool I genuinely use on my own projects.

projects.name: ClientSync
projects.description: Responsive client-management system spanning four modules — clients, projects, invoices and payments — with an Express.js/Node.js backend, 5+ RESTful APIs with full CRUD operations and dashboard analytics, plus a React + Tailwind CSS front end that stays consistent across screen sizes.
projects.details:
A client-management system for tracking the full lifecycle of freelance-style work — from the first client contact to the final payment.

Four connected modules: Clients (contacts and communication history), Projects (status and assignment), Invoices (billing documents) and Payments (tracking what's been collected) — so money never slips through the cracks.

The backend is Express.js/Node.js exposing 5+ RESTful APIs with full CRUD operations, plus analytics endpoints that power the dashboard's charts. The frontend is React + Vite with Tailwind CSS, carefully made responsive so it works on phone, tablet and desktop.

Source code: github.com/vivekchowdarythondapu/clientsync

achievements.title: IEEE Conference Paper Author
achievements.description: "X-Stroke: An Explainable AI-Using Machine Learning Model for Heart Stroke Prediction" published at ICoECIT 2026 (IEEE Xplore).
achievements.details:
My research paper "X-Stroke: An Explainable AI-Based Machine Learning Model for Heart Stroke Prediction" was accepted and presented at the IEEE International Conference on Emerging Computing and Intelligent Technologies (ICoECIT 2026), held 28–29 January 2026 — with IEEE Conference Record Number 68303.

The work grew out of my Research Internship at GNITS: applying ML classification algorithms to medical datasets to predict heart-stroke risk, building preprocessing and feature-selection pipelines, and wrapping the model in explainable-AI so doctors can understand *why* a prediction was made — not just what it was.

The certificate shown was awarded to our presenting author, my mentor G.V Vidhya Lakshmi, who presented the paper on behalf of the team at the conference.

highlights: Developed a machine-learning research project on Heart Stroke Prediction, applying classification algorithms to medical datasets
Built data preprocessing and feature-selection pipelines that improved model accuracy and reliability across multiple algorithms
Optimized model performance through iterative testing, contributing to a published IEEE conference paper (ICoECIT 2026)
